title: Duchy of Bytom
capsule: The Duchy of Bytom was a small Upper Silesian Piast appanage created around 1284–1285 when Casimir of Bytom became sole ruler after jointly governing with his brother Bolko I of Opole. Under pressure from conflict with his Piast cousin Henryk IV Probus, Casimir in 1289 became the first Silesian Piast duke to submit to Bohemian overlordship, placing Bytom under the Přemyslid crown — a precedent that accelerated the broader Bohemian absorption of Silesian duchies across the fourteenth century. Around 1303 the duchy shed the territories of Koźle and Toszek as separate units. Casimir died in 1312; the duchy continued under his son Siemowit before the male line's extinction in 1355 triggered inheritance disputes that eventually merged Bytom with the Duchy of Opole by 1498.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's political history is documented through Bohemian and Polish charters, but its precise territorial footprint in the 1285–1305 window is approximate, as Silesian boundaries shifted frequently with each sub-partition of Piast holdings.
